stances.claim: The SBN's outright dismissal of Civil Case No. 0002 -- based on the OSG/PCGG's failure to prove allegations by preponderance of evidence and submission of barely-readable photocopies -- looks bad in isolation but is misleading without Justice Mañalac's corrective separate opinion.

stances.claim: Justice Mañalac is correct, 'in my humble opinion,' that the bulk of the litigated assets in Civil Case No. 0002 had already been recovered by the State via prior SC final judgments and PCGG compromises -- making 'the Republic had proven its case by more than [a] preponderance of evidence' the truer picture.
stances.rhetorical_move: concurrence-as-truth elevation (the separate opinion captures reality the ponencia missed)

stances.claim: The Dec 6, 2005 SBN resolution finding 'prima facie presumption that the assets and properties in this case are ill-gotten' -- never reversed or modified by the SC in Republic v. Marcos-Manotoc (Feb 8, 2012) -- survives, and the PCGG's failure to address it in their memorandum is a glaring omission.
stances.rhetorical_move: underused-resolution surfacing (an unreversed prima facie finding is the most powerful overlooked instrument)

stances.claim: The PCGG should file a motion for reconsideration that clarifies -- for the SBN and 'our disgruntled people' -- which of the litigated assets remain outstanding after subtracting those already recovered through Swiss-deposit forfeiture, PTIC reconveyance, Arelma forfeiture, jewelry forfeiture, Campos turnover, and the Floirendo/Cuenca/Benedicto compromises.
stances.rhetorical_move: constructive-MR prescription (turning a public defeat into a recoverable record)

stances.claim: Given the PCGG's documented P172B+ recovery since 1986, the agency is 'not that inutile' as public perception holds, and this 'monumental P200 billion ill-gotten wealth case' filed in its 'early hallelujah days' 'was not dismally and sloppily lost.'
stances.rhetorical_move: public-perception correction (defending an unloved institution against its own headlines)

The catalogue of recovered Marcos assets sequenced chronologically (2003 Swiss, 2006 PTIC, 2012 Arelma, 2017 jewelry, plus Campos turnover, plus the Floirendo/Cuenca/Benedicto compromises) -- used as cumulative evidence that the case 'was not dismally and sloppily lost.'

CJ's self-disclosure 'some during my term' -- flagging that he himself wrote the 2003 Swiss-deposits forfeiture; the personal stake in defending the cumulative recovery record is left implicit but unmistakable.
The 'hallelujah days' phrase for the early PCGG -- a single phrase capturing both the post-EDSA optimism and the subsequent institutional decline into the perception of inutility.
The closing line -- '... not dismally and sloppily lost' -- the most carefully cadenced double-negative defense in CJ's writing on the Marcos recovery effort.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban defends the P200-billion ill-gotten wealth case in Civil Case No. 0002 -- dismissed by the Sandiganbayan on Dec 16, 2019 after 32 years of wearying litigation -- against the public verdict that it was 'dismally and sloppily lost.' The ponencia by Justice Alex L. Quiroz faulted the PCGG for failing to prove its allegations by preponderance of evidence, citing barely-readable photocopies and the best-evidence rule. But Justices Mendoza-Arcega and Mañalac concurred only 'in the result,' and Mañalac's separate opinion -- 'correctly in my humble opinion' -- pointed out that the bulk of the litigated assets had already been received by the State via compromise or favorable judgment in related cases. CJ catalogues: the 2003 Swiss-deposit forfeiture of US$658M+ (penned during his own term), the 2006 reconveyance of 111,415 PTIC controlling shares (PLDT's biggest shareholder), the 2012 Arelma Inc. NY forfeiture of $3M+, the 2017 forfeiture of the Malacañang jewelry collection, the voluntary Campos turnover, and the Floirendo/Cuenca/Benedicto compromises. Mañalac also exhumed the 'little known' Dec 6, 2005 SBN resolution finding prima facie presumption that the assets are ill-gotten -- never reversed by the SC in Marcos-Manotoc (Feb 8, 2012). The PCGG's memorandum 'did not bother to address' which assets remain outstanding. CJ recommends a motion for reconsideration to clarify the residual -- easy to do, given the PCGG's documented P172B+ recovery since 1986 -- proving the agency is 'not that inutile' as public perception holds, and this monumental case from its 'early hallelujah days' was not dismally and sloppily lost.
